pattern: A tooling migration landed as doc edits (CLAUDE.md says br is the tracker) while the data lane was never materialized (no issues.jsonl, cited migration record absent, br errors) — leaving the repo with NO working tracker under a no-bead-no-PR doctrine
detection_question: Does every doc claim of a completed migration have a verifiable on-disk artifact (the new tool actually runs, the cited record exists)?
checklist_item: Before committing migration docs, run the new tool end-to-end and verify every file path the doc cites exists

pattern: A data migration/import was one git add away from publishing private cross-context data (full bead ledger: client, SOC, fleet topology) to a PUBLIC repo — every plan artifact inherited the 'commit the JSONL' assumption without ever checking remote visibility
detection_question: Before any arc that commits a data store: is the remote public, and does the data carry content from more-private contexts (imports inherit the privacy ceiling of their most sensitive source)?
checklist_item: Run gh repo view --json visibility,isPrivate and classify the data BEFORE staging any migrated/imported store; default ledgers to a private nested repo or gitignore

pattern: A gate that greps literal wording in a doc (19b closeout contract) forms a coupled chain with that doc: editing the doc without flipping the gate in the SAME commit red-mains every push — hit twice in one day (bd->br flip, private-ledger amendment)
detection_question: Does any gate script literally assert strings in the doc I am editing (grep gate scripts for the doc name + grep -Fq patterns)?
checklist_item: Before editing doctrine docs, find gates asserting them; ship doc+gate atomically and prove PASS-on-new/FAIL-on-old via fixture before pushing

pattern: An epic body enumerating N targets but decomposed into <N child beads closes green on children-all-closed while the unfiled targets silently evaporate (ag-p273x: 7 targets, 5 children — target 5 recovered only by a close-time body-vs-children diff)
detection_question: Does the epic body enumerate more scope items (targets/findings/bullets) than it has child beads, and does each item have a disposition (LANDED sha / SCHEDULED bead / DROPPED reason)?
checklist_item: At epic close, diff the epic body s enumerated scope against the child set and record one disposition per item on the epic before closing; children-all-closed is necessary, not sufficient

pattern: A pre-mortem names the right risk, the mitigation ships with green byte-exact tests, but the fixture never contains the failure trigger (ag-48ybr: comment-eating risk predicted; fixture had no comment adjacent to the edited row; adversarial judge running the real binary found 5 defects incl. 2 MEDIUM)
detection_question: For each pre-mortem risk row, does some test fixture contain the actual failure trigger (the adjacent comment, the EOF row, the hostile flag value) — not just the mitigation happy path?
checklist_item: Per pre-mortem risk: name the trigger and require a fixture containing it; for new file-mutating CLI commands, split the 2-judge council into acceptance roll-up + hostile-input behavioral judge on the real binary

pattern: An orchestrator brief specifies a contract (schema/format/hash spec) from memory instead of citing the contract file; the spec is wrong and a stochastic worker may trust the brief over the file (ag-8jf97: hash-spec brief contradicted the committed schema, nearly broke the chain)
detection_question: Does this implementer brief restate a schema/format/contract from memory instead of pointing at the contract file and saying the contract wins?
checklist_item: Every build-against-X brief links the contract file + states contracts-win-over-brief; never re-derive the spec from memory

pattern: Verifying a failure-detector (tamper check, fail-closed gate) without actually inducing the failure AND confirming the harness induced it -> false pass or false alarm (ag-8jf97: BSD sed silently no-op tamper -> verify falsely flagged PROBLEM on an untouched ledger; pipe-masked exit codes)
detection_question: Did I confirm the failure was actually induced (grep the injected marker) and capture the real exit code (not through a pipe) before believing the detector catches it?
checklist_item: To verify a lie-detector: induce the failure, grep-confirm it landed, capture exit via cmd;rc=$? (never |head;$?), believe only after watching it fail on cue

pattern: codex exec "<positional prompt>" in any non-TTY context (background, ATM/NTM pane, cron, nohup) reads from stdin and hangs forever on 'Reading additional input from stdin...'; the pane looks alive but never starts the task (orchestration-spike 2026-06-15)
detection_question: Is any codex exec being launched in a non-interactive context (background/&, tmux/ATM pane, cron, nohup) without closing or feeding stdin?
checklist_item: In non-TTY contexts, never pass the prompt positionally bare: pipe it (printf '%s' "$P" | codex exec) or append </dev/null so codex does not block reading stdin

pattern: atm/ntm spawn returns before the pane agent has booted to its input box; a send issued in the first few seconds is silently dropped — the pane looks spawned but the agent never engages, and the operator wedges it by dispatching too early (orchestration-spike 2026-06-15). This is operator error, not a tool defect.
detection_question: Does the first send/dispatch to a freshly spawned pane gate on a readiness signal, or does it fire on a fixed/zero delay assuming spawn==ready?
checklist_item: After spawn, gate the first dispatch on readiness: atm codex preflight / wait-goal-engaged for codex panes, or wait-for-ready before any send; never send in the first few seconds on a bare delay

pattern: atm save / tmux capture-pane of a codex TUI returns mostly ANSI escape sequences that strip to empty; the documented 'read the pane' fallback gives a false-empty and you cannot tell idle from working by reading text (orchestration-spike 2026-06-15)
detection_question: Am I judging a codex pane's liveness by captured pane text (which is ANSI-blind for a TUI) instead of process/artifact ground truth?
checklist_item: For codex-pane liveness use ground truth, not capture text: pane-PID ps CPU%% (0.0%% + no new artifact = idle), expected output artifacts on disk, and atm codex palette-state --json

pattern: Pointed a heavy ATM swarm at a tiny one-shot task (generate 9 content ideas) that wanted in-session Agent fan-out; the swarm wedged and cost more setup+recovery than doing it inline would have (orchestration-spike 2026-06-15)
detection_question: Before standing up a swarm: is this reusable automation or a one-shot, and does it have >=2 independent working-tree units of work? If one-shot or single-unit, why is a swarm involved?
checklist_item: Gate every swarm on: (1) reusable automation, not one-shot, AND (2) >=2 independent working-tree units. One-shot or single-unit -> do it inline (in-session Agent fan-out or just do it), do NOT orchestrate

pattern: When a sibling repo or external subsystem is archived, consumer repos often keep live-looking docs, skills, scripts, executable flags, and tracker items that still route work through the retired surface.
detection_question: After archiving or retiring a repo/substrate, did we grep the consuming repo for the retired names across first-read docs, skills, scripts, generated help, code validation, and tracker queues?
checklist_item: Run a downstream reconciliation sweep for archived repo names and route aliases; retarget, banner as historical, or close/supersede each live-looking consumer before calling the archive definitive.
